The prevalence of incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) has been shown to be significant. However, research suggests that obesity may be a contributing factor in this phenomenon.

The study found that patients with higher body mass index (BMI) and those who are overweight or obese have an increased likelihood of developing idiopathic misty mesentery on CT scans compared to those with normal BMI. Additionally, the growing evidence of obesity-induced inflammatory changes in adipose tissue may also play a role in the development of this condition.

Furthermore, studies have shown that patients with higher BMIs tend to develop more severe and complex forms of misty mesenteritis. This suggests that obesity may be acting as a trigger for the development of idiopathic misty mesentery on MDCT scans.

It's essential to note that while obesity is a contributing factor in the development of misty mesentery, it is not the sole cause. The exact mechanisms by which obesity leads to misty mesenteritis are still unclear and require further research.

In conclusion, the presence of idiopathic misty mesentery on MDCT scans can be influenced by obesity, but it is not the only factor involved in its development. Further studies are needed to fully understand the relationship between obesity and misty mesentery.
